summary: A Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and taught Bhikkhu Bodhi. He served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society from circa 1958 to 1984.

Specializing in Tibetology, Nyingcha Duoji studied at Boston University and earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, committee member Janet Gyatso, and teacher Mark C. Elliott.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Katok Monastery and under Penor Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught numerous students, including Douglas S. Duckworth and Sogyal Rinpoche.
A Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, he earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) under Ernst Steinkellner. He subsequently held a professorship at the University of Hamburg.

An archaeology and history scholar, he studied at the University of Paris (~1946–1948), Harvard (~1948–1950), and Princeton (~1950–1955). He held faculty posts at the University of Michigan (~1954–1969) and Harvard (~1969–1990).

An Indology and history/archaeology scholar, he was Secretary at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede and Betty Heimann. He chaired Sanskrit at Ceylon, taught at Smith College, and held visiting roles at Penn and Harvard.
A scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

A scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, he studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1925–1939). He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, he studied at Copenhagen, Washington, and Harvard under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner. He served as ansvarig utgivare at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, he completed his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad. He taught at Kirori Mal College (attested 1961) and served as professor of economic history at Delhi (attested 2003).

A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, she studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. She held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and Hamburg (attested 2007).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at Hamburg (1992). He was assistant professor (1979–1984) and professor (1995–2003) at Nagasaki, and professor at Shiga University of Medical Science (2003–2013) and Ryukoku (2013–2015).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied under Baiei Henmi. He served as director of the fine arts department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
An Indologist who studied at the University of Turin (~1941–1945). He was the founder of the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

An Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar, he completed his Habilitation at Mainz (~1968–1973) and studied under Paul Thieme. He held professorships at Mainz (~1973–1981) and Freiburg (~1981–2006) and directed the Nepal Research Centre.
A scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, he studied under Paul Bernard (~1983–1987). He held a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (attested 2015).
Specializing in sinology and history/archaeology, he studied at the University of Helsinki (~1897–1900). He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and the Nationalmuseum (1928–1945).
An Indologist, philosopher, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar, he studied at Paris and London. He held professorships at Bamberg (~1804–1807), Würzburg (~1821–1826), and Munich (1826).
